title: Kingdom of Gwent
capsule: Gwent was a Welsh kingdom occupying the lowlands between the rivers Wye and Usk in southeast Wales, its name derived from the Roman civitas capital Venta Silurum (Caerwent). Tracing its ruling dynasty to post-Roman magnates, it was periodically united with neighbouring Glywysing to form the larger entity of Morgannwg. Gruffydd ap Llywelyn conquered Gwent around 1055 in his brief unification of Wales; after his death in 1063 the kingdom re-emerged briefly before being overrun by Norman Marcher lords from 1067 onward, who partitioned it into lordships based at Chepstow, Monmouth, and Abergavenny and ended Welsh dynastic rule by the 1090s.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Gwent's general territory between the Wye and Usk is established in Welsh genealogical records and Norman conquest documents, but internal subdivisions and exact royal boundaries are poorly attested.
